components.description: For a primary-caregiver tenured or tenure-track parent with 12 months of employment: a two-course reduction of in-classroom teaching in one semester (the birth/placement term or the next), at full salary; advising and administrative duties continue (off campus).
components.mechanism_note: Called a leave, but it consists of a two-course reduction of in-classroom instruction at full salary with advising and administrative duties continuing: relief on active service (modified duties), not a leave of absence.
components.faculty_group_note: University full-time tenured or tenure-track faculty members (Faculty Handbook 2013, D.30; the Handbook covers Dyson College of Arts and Sciences, Seidenberg (computer science), Lubin, Education, Health Professions and Law)
components.eligible_parent_wording: "become parents (through birth, or by adoption or newly established legal custodial care involving a child younger than 6 years of age)"; "Parent is defined as a natural parent, same-sex partner, or a new adoptive parent or a new legal custodian who is the primary caregiver."; "An individual who adopts a spouse or partner’s child(ren) is not eligible for this benefit."
components.caregiver_condition_wording: Primary Caregiver is defined as someone who has primary responsibility for the care of a child immediately following birth. The faculty member determines who in his or her family the primary caregiver is by signing an affidavit as part of the leave request process.
components.entitlement_note: 'are eligible for the Faculty Parental Leave' and 'shall consist of': the policy gives the reduction; the request (with the caregiver affidavit) covers the arrangements (V2).
components.duration_note: Two courses of in-classroom instruction, in one semester; course reductions are not converted to weeks (R11b). The Handbook sets a teaching load of 18 credit hours a year for tenure-track faculty and 18 or 24 for tenured faculty (D.16), so two courses are part of a semester's load.
components.relief_note: In-classroom instruction reduced by two courses in one semester; advising and other administrative duties continue as the chair determines, but need not be on campus; research and clinical duties are not named (continue, R4b).
components.time_window: during the academic term (Spring or Fall semester) in which the birth, adoption or new legal custodial care occurs, or the term immediately following; adoption or custodial care of a child younger than 6 years of age
components.notice: caregiver affidavit signed as part of the leave request process

notes: Reference date 2018-02-27. The Faculty Handbook 2013 Edition is the governing document for faculty (version note: in force on the reference date; the next edition is from 2024). The HR Leaves page is a Wayback capture of 2018-03-09, within the reference academic year; its Faculty section repeats the Handbook's sabbatical, scholarly and parental-leave texts ('Source: 2013 Faculty Handbook'), and it supplies the Maternity and short-term disability terms the Handbook leaves to HR (the Handbook lists 'short-term and long-term disability insurance' among benefits and refers to the Benefits Office for details). Maternity is therefore not flagged summary_only.
missing is false: the Faculty Handbook is a governing faculty handbook covering tenure-stream faculty and contains the Faculty Parental Leave Policy, tenure clock stoppage and leaves.

The HR page's Staff section repeats the Faculty section's Maternity, Bereavement, Jury Duty, Military and Family and Medical Leave texts; these are the same provisions (c2-c5 cover 'full time employees'), not separate components. Staff-only: Personal leave (c11) and the NY Paid Family Leave it names (c12, c13).

Path (U8): the member with two years of service is in the '12 Months and Over' salary-continuation band (full base salary up to 26 weeks). Other paths: 3-12 months, first two months full base salary then up to four months half salary; under 3 months, no University continuation and 'Eligible for the NYS Disability benefit only' (NY Disability Benefits Law, not coded as a component for this member).

Not components: bereavement (death), jury duty, military leave (USERRA), sabbatical and scholarly leaves (professional projects), leave for doctoral study completion (degree completion), tenure clock stoppage for extraordinary circumstances (D.7(c): strikes, epidemics, disasters), and D.7(a)'s general caregiver clause, whose newborn case is the automatic stoppage c7 (specific provision governs) and whose other cases (a parent, spouse or partner in a health crisis) are folded into c7's note rather than coded separately.
Faculty Parental Leave (c1) is a two-course reduction in one semester at full salary; course reductions are recorded without a week count (R11b), so it adds no weeks to the 2018-definition figure.

Calendar: 'Academic Term is defined as the Spring or Fall semester' (kind of term stated, length not stated) -> calendar.kind = semester, and the term length follows R8's order. The Handbook also says 'The two-semester academic year shall consist of not more than thirty-six weeks' (a maximum, not a term length).

Chain, birth parent: short-term disability leave c3 (up to 26 weeks) from the start, containing the maternity childbirth benefit c2 (6, up to 8 weeks, full base salary) and the STD salary continuation c4 (up to 26 weeks, full pay; generic plan), with FMLA c5 (12 workweeks) concurrent from the start -> return-to-duty assignment c10 (other, not counted) consecutive_after c3. Course reduction c1 (two courses in the birth term or the next) and tenure clock stoppage c7 (one year) are unlinked.

Chain, non-birth parent: FMLA c5 (12 workweeks) -> return-to-duty assignment c10 (other) consecutive_after c5; course reduction c1 (if primary caregiver) and tenure clock stoppage c7 (if primarily responsible for care) unlinked.

Cross-references not saved: Pace Family and Medical Leave Policy; How to Report a Short-Term Disability Claim and/or Family Medical Leave (FML); Employee Rights and Responsibilities Under the FMLA; Sick Leave policy (Handbook D.15); short- and long-term disability Summary Plan Documents; Law School Faculty Handbook (Law School only); Union of Adjunct Faculty at Pace collective agreement (adjuncts only); Pace Policy Against Discrimination, Harassment and Retaliation; Provost's annual promotion and tenure statement.
